after:
- run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - name: fetch the records branches the guard may read
        # The log at this head is main's log at branch time and trails the
        # primary checkout's live log, so a grant tapped during the session
        # reaches a committed log only when an advance lands (APRV-260). The
        # guard therefore reads the freshest committed copy that carries THIS
        # head's own chain, and those copies live on `records-*` branches.
        # `fetch-depth: 0` already brings them; this makes the dependency
        # explicit rather than resting on checkout's default refspec, and it
        # names no untrusted context value at all.
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin '+refs/heads/records-*:refs/remotes/origin/records-*'
      - name: cross-check protected paths against the committed log
        # Context values reach the script as environment variables and are never
        # interpolated into its text, for the reason the classify job states: a
        # branch name is attacker-shaped input and must not become shell syntax.
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ] && [ -n "$BASE_REF" ]; then
            target="origin/$BASE_REF"
          else
            target="origin/main"
          fi
          base="$(git merge-base "$target" HEAD)"
          echo "base=$base head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          # The guard's first line says which committed copy of the log it read
          # and how far past head that copy reaches; it is repeated into the job
          # summary so a reader can tell a stale log from a missing grant
          # without opening the log.
          node scripts/protected-path-guard.mjs --base "$base" --head HEAD | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/guard.txt"
          grep '^log from ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/guard.txt" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
